prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, from bifunctional PROTACs to the molecular mechanism of thalidomide-type glue degraders

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical mode of action: a small molecule acts as a bridge that recruits an E3 ligase, so the cell's own non-equilibrium machinery removes the target instead of the molecule merely occupying a site. It has the broadest conceptual reach on the shortlist, since it opens the so-called undruggable proteome and explains the mechanism of thalidomide-class drugs. It is also the candidate with the widest and most robust opening support, with first-place votes from three members and top-three placements from six, and the support comes from members with very different scientific backgrounds. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs, and Handa's identification of cereblon supplies the glue mechanism, so the three together span concept and mechanism. Independent confirmation across many labs is extensive, and clinical degraders are in late-stage trials.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the committee could reasonably argue that the field is a few years early. Credit is spread over at least eight named people, and a three-person cap excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Ito, each with a real claim. The PROTAC and molecular-glue strands have different histories, and a single citation may blur two distinct achievements. If the committee finds that blur unacceptable, a prize centred on a mature, fully validated method such as genetic code expansion (B054) is the safer choice.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B068) first, as a general, decades-old, industrially proven method with a clean Buchwald/Hartwig two-person attribution, and notes that the 2010 prize did not cover C-N coupling.
responses.response: I accept the attribution is cleaner than for B057, and I accept the maturity argument, which is stronger than anything I can say for degraders. My reservation is that, after 2010, a second prize on cross-coupling invites the objection that it extends a recognised field with an additional bond type, whereas induced-proximity pharmacology is a new mode of action. B068 is only on three members' ballots, and I put it outside my top eight, so I will not move it ahead of B057 unless the committee agrees that general scope and priority clarity should outweigh novelty. I would keep it as a strong reserve option and want to hear whether Peter sees C-N coupling as conceptually distinct from the 2010 work.

responses.point: Brzezinski and Aqvist both put Ciulli, not Handa, alongside Crews and Deshaies, because Ciulli gave the VHL ligand and ternary-complex structural basis, and Brzezinski warns that the cereblon glue story may deserve separate recognition.
responses.response: This is the most serious attribution issue for B057 and I do not think my Crews, Deshaies and Handa cut is settled. Ciulli's VHL work made PROTACs drug-like and gave the structural understanding of ternary complexes, which is real chemistry. I still lean towards Handa because cereblon explains a long-standing pharmacological puzzle and unites the glue and bifunctional strands under one mechanism, while Ciulli's contribution is an enabling refinement of the PROTAC strand. I do not hold this firmly, and I would take Ciulli over Deshaies if the committee prefers to centre the prize on bifunctional degraders. I disagree with splitting the field into two prizes now, since that would use the whole prize on one area.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates (B005) first, as a reframing of intracellular organisation as a physical-chemical phase-separation problem, and ranks B057 only fourth because clinical proof is still maturing.
responses.response: I agree that the polymer and colloid physics in condensates is conceptually significant and the confirmation is strong. My concern is the one Emma also raises, that it is still debated which in vivo condensates are truly phase-separated and functionally relevant, and credit is split among five serious names with Pappu and Mittag as plausible alternatives. Daniel also asks whether it counts as chemistry in the prize sense. Compared with that, the degradation mechanism is established at the molecular level even though clinical validation is incomplete. Only two members ranked B005 at all, so I would want to see stronger support from the physical-chemistry side before moving it up.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B057 first with the Crews, Deshaies and Handa cut, but notes that the lack of an approved degrader may argue for waiting, and also puts base editing (B016) in the top three with a Liu-centred attribution.
responses.response: I agree on the cut and share the worry about timing, but I do not think the committee has traditionally required an approved drug when the mechanism and generality are confirmed across many laboratories. On B016, I take Andrei's point that the genome-editing field was recognised in 2020 and that Liu also leads the prime-editing candidate, so a base-editing prize may be better framed together with that work if it is pursued. I would keep B016 as an alternative and not as my first choice.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands as one achievement or require two distinct recipients
Whether Handa or Ciulli should take the third place beside Crews and Deshaies
Whether the lack of an approved degrader makes the prize premature
Whether post-2010 recognition of C-N coupling (B068) is judged more valuable than a new modality because of its maturity and clean attribution
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile; none of the named people is a documented collaborator or Lund colleague. As chair I note that two fellow Lund academics, Somfai and Sparr, sit on the committee, but this does not bear on any candidate here.
